Li diffuses through the rigid sulfur framework with a thermally activated tracer diffusion coefficient. The activation energy is about 0.29 eV, from five 10 ps runs at 500–900 K. The Arrhenius plot is saved as `arrhenius.png`.

**Method.** I computed the per-species MSD of each run (0.01 ps between frames, 128 atoms in a 16 Å cubic cell, 64 Li and 64 S). The Li MSD is close to linear beyond about 1 ps. I took D from a linear fit over lags of 1–5 ps (cell 4 for T500, cell 6 for all five runs).

**Results.**

| T (K) | D_Li (Å²/ps) | D_Li (cm²/s) |
|---|---|---|
| 500 | 0.0298 | 2.98 × 10⁻⁶ |
| 600 | 0.115 | 1.15 × 10⁻⁵ |
| 700 | 0.255 | 2.55 × 10⁻⁵ |
| 800 | 0.362 | 3.62 × 10⁻⁵ |
| 900 | 0.599 | 5.99 × 10⁻⁵ |

- The Arrhenius fit gives Ea = 0.285 ± 0.018 eV and D0 = 2.5 × 10⁻³ cm²/s (R² = 0.988; cell 9, plot in cell 11).
- Across four fit windows, Ea stays between 0.275 and 0.285 eV (cell 10).
- The S MSD is indistinguishable from zero (|D_S| ≤ 5 × 10⁻⁶ Å²/ps), so Li is the only mobile species.

**Caveats.** Each run is only 10 ps with 64 Li, so the D values carry a few percent of statistical scatter. The five points also show slight curvature (ln D residuals up to about ±0.14), so Ea should be read as indicative. I did not run a site-hopping analysis, so the hop mechanism is not resolved. A SiteHopping analysis on the Li trajectories would give the jump distances and residence times needed to identify it.

**Paragraph for the results section:**

Li self-diffusion was obtained from 10 ps NVT ab initio MD runs at 500, 600, 700, 800 and 900 K (2 fs time step; 128-atom cells with 64 Li and 64 S). The Li mean-squared displacement is linear beyond about 1 ps. The tracer diffusion coefficient from a linear fit over 1–5 ps lags is D(500 K) = 2.98 × 10⁻⁶ cm²/s, rising to 1.15 × 10⁻⁵, 2.55 × 10⁻⁵, 3.62 × 10⁻⁵ and 5.99 × 10⁻⁵ cm²/s at 600–900 K.
